meta_title: Area in First Quadrant: Line, x-axis & Circle | Ex 8.1 Q6
meta_desc: NCERT Class 12 Ex 8.1 Q6 solved: first-quadrant area bounded by the x-axis, x=√3 y and the circle x²+y²=4. See the steps, then take a free quiz.

quiz.title: Application of Integrals Quiz
quiz.intro: Eight questions on area under a curve, area between curves and circular sectors. Choose an answer for each, then press Check my score.
quiz.about: Class 12 Application of Integrals: area under and between curves

questions.q: The area under a curve y = f(x) from x = a to x = b (with f(x) ≥ 0) is given by:
options: ∫ from a to b of x dy
∫ from a to b of f(x) dx
∫ from a to b of f'(x) dx
questions.explanation: Area = ∫ from a to b of y dx = ∫ from a to b of f(x) dx when the curve lies above the x-axis.

questions.q: The area of the region enclosed by the circle x² + y² = 4 is:
In NCERT Ex 8.1 Q6, the line x = √3 y makes what angle with the positive x-axis?
questions.explanation: x = √3 y means y = x/√3, so slope = 1/√3 = tan 30°. The line is at 30° to the x-axis.

questions.q: The line x = √3 y meets the circle x² + y² = 4 (first quadrant) at:
questions.explanation: Substitute x = √3 y: 3y² + y² = 4, so y² = 1, y = 1 and x = √3. The point is (√3, 1).

questions.q: ∫ from 0 to 2 of √(4 − x²) dx equals:
questions.explanation: This is a quarter of the circle of radius 2. Using ∫√(a²−x²)dx, the value from 0 to 2 is π.

questions.q: The area of the region in Ex 8.1 Q6 (first quadrant, bounded by x-axis, x = √3 y and the circle) is:
questions.explanation: Split at x = √3: area = ∫ from 0 to √3 of (x/√3) dx + ∫ from √3 to 2 of √(4−x²) dx = √3/2 + (π/3 − √3/2) = π/3.

questions.q: The area between two curves y = f(x) (upper) and y = g(x) (lower) from a to b is:
questions.explanation: Area between curves = ∫ from a to b of (upper − lower) dx = ∫ [f(x) − g(x)] dx.

questions.q: The area of the ellipse x²/a² + y²/b² = 1 is:
questions.explanation: By integrating, the total area of the ellipse works out to πab; when a = b = r it reduces to the circle area πr².

faq.q: What region does NCERT Ex 8.1 Q6 ask about?
faq.a: It asks for the area in the first quadrant that is enclosed by the x-axis, the line x = √3 y, and the circle x² + y² = 4. It is a wedge of the circle between the x-axis and the line.
The line x = √3 y sits at 30° to the x-axis, so the region is a 30° sector of a circle of radius 2. A full circle has area 4π, and 30° is one-twelfth of 360°, giving 4π/12 = π/3.

faq.q: How do you set up the integral for this problem?
faq.a: Find where the line meets the circle at (√3, 1), then split the x-range. From x = 0 to √3 the top boundary is the line y = x/√3; from x = √3 to 2 the top boundary is the circle y = √(4−x²). Add the two integrals.

faq.q: Where does the point (√3, 1) come from?
faq.a: Substitute x = √3 y into x² + y² = 4 to get 4y² = 4, so y = 1 and x = √3. That intersection is where you switch the upper boundary from the line to the circle.
